nodes.description: The two dominant Klippel-Feil forms act through GDF6 and GDF3 rather than through the MEOX1 transcription factor. GDF6 is expressed at the boundaries of the developing vertebrae, carpals and tarsals, and losing it in mouse and Xenopus reproduces fusion at those boundaries together with anterior axial defects, so this node is a defect of skeletal boundary patterning rather than of the cervical spine alone. GDF3 is a paralogue investigated for the same reason, and its mutation perturbs BMP signalling.

nodes.description: Loss of MEOX1, a homeobox transcription factor with a nonredundant role in somite development, disrupts sclerotome polarity and the somite-boundary / resegmentation program in the paraxial mesoderm. KFS is the human phenotypic equivalent of the sclerotome polarity defect seen in Meox1-null mice. The dominant GDF6- and GDF3-related forms are carried on the separate BMP ligand node below, and the recessive MYO18B-related form on its own node.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function MYO18B alleles are degraded by nonsense-mediated decay, leaving no functional myosin XVIIIB. ClinGen's expert-panel summary reads the disease mechanism as homozygous loss of function. The deficiency yields the Klippel-Feil anomaly together with a myopathy, facial dysmorphism and short stature, so it is the one Klippel-Feil lesion whose consequences reach outside the axial skeleton.
